correctness.rationale: Every cone distance from a fixed radial point reduces to a Euclidean chord in the angle-minimizing convex sector. The disk-sector area identity is exact. Disjoint circular caps give the intermediate branch; polar integration gives the apex-entering branch. Exact first and second derivatives establish a 3/2 onset and a positive 2 tan(beta) second-derivative jump, while analytic open branches exclude any other positive singular radii. Inversion uses sin(beta)=d/s and tan(beta)=J/2 on the strict domain beta in (0,pi/2). The saved standard-library checker independently evaluated 70 finite cases; these checks are diagnostic and the analytic argument proves all real-parameter cases.

value.rationale: The geodesic ball-area profile is a canonical intrinsic local measurement used in metric geometry; unlike small-radius smooth curvature expansions it encounters a cut locus and then a cone apex at distinguishable positive radii. The result gives a complete sharp two-contact classification and a finite-data inverse geometric signature of cone opening and radial location, with the precise 3/2 law and second-derivative jump. It is a natural exact structural theorem, not a reparameterized numeric benchmark or a finite computation.
